concepts.title: The Sun Lifts Water Up
concepts.explanation: The sun warms water in oceans, lakes and puddles. The warm water turns into a gas called water vapor. You can't see it, but it rises into the sky. This is called evaporation.
concepts.example: A puddle on the playground slowly gets smaller on a sunny day.

concepts.title: Clouds Are Made of Water
concepts.explanation: High in the sky, the air is cold. The water vapor cools down and turns back into tiny drops of water. Lots of drops together make a cloud. This is called condensation.
concepts.example: Drops form on the outside of a cold glass of lemonade.

concepts.title: Water Falls and Collects
concepts.explanation: When cloud drops join and get heavy, they fall as rain, snow or hail. This is called precipitation. The water collects in oceans, lakes and rivers. Then the cycle starts again.
concepts.example: Rain fills a bucket you leave outside.

questions.question: What makes water rise into the sky?
options: The sun warms it into water vapor
questions.why: Warmth from the sun turns water into vapor, and the vapor rises. That's evaporation!

questions.question: What is a cloud made of?
questions.why: Water vapor cools into tiny drops, and lots of drops make a cloud.

questions.question: Rain, snow and hail are all kinds of what?
questions.why: Water falling from clouds is called precipitation.

questions.question: Drops form on a cold glass of lemonade. Which step is this like?
questions.why: Vapor in the air cools when it touches the cold glass and turns into drops, just like in a cloud.

questions.question: Where does rain water collect?
questions.why: Rain collects in oceans, lakes and rivers, and then the cycle starts again.
